summary: Intermittent p99 latency spikes traced to prefix-merge lag in multi-tenant coalescer
description:
Issue summary: NimbusDocs reports intermittent p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s for short streaming requests originating from their us-east dedicated cluster. Impact: customer-facing application experiences brief user-facing freezes (~5-20s) multiple times per hour, causing support tickets and reduction in session throughput. Environment: prod, dedicated pool for NimbusDocs (tenant id: nimbus-47), serving runtime 1.8.2, coalescer service v0.9.1. Observed window: first seen 2026-03-11 22:10 UTC; recurring through 2026-03-12.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer exercises short streaming completions (prompt length ~10 tokens, expected response ~30 tokens) at sustained 12 rps per connection across 120 concurrent connections.
2) A mix of shorter single-turn and occasional long-turn (>512 tokens) requests present.
3) Intermittent p99 spikes observed in per-route dashboards and SLO alerts.

Observed behavior:
- p95 stable ~120ms, p99 jumps to 2.5s-7s for brief epochs (~30–90s).
- Streaming sessions show delayed first-chunk arrivals and sporadic 504s.
- Batch size distribution shows sudden microbatching where many 10-token requests are held until a long request arrives.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous coalescer should maintain sub-300ms first-chunk latency for short streaming requests under this load profile.

Logs/metrics/attachments:
- Grafana panels: per-tenant p99, batch-size histogram, coalescer flush latency.
- Traces: sample trace ids attached in comments.
- Customer provided client logs showing client-side time-to-first-chunk latency spikes.

Notes: customer is on Dedicated and has strict SLA requirements. They reported the issue via support chat and attached a short repro script that simulates their traffic mix.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage completed. Confirmed p99 spikes from NimbusDocs route. Reached out to SRE on-call and opened this ticket. Asking customer for request traces and sample payloads.

2026-03-12 10:02 - Luca Moreno (SRE): Acknowledged. Spun up additional per-tenant coalescer debug logging and enabled trace sampling for tenant nimbus-47. Noted correlated increase in "coalescer_flush_delay_ms" metric aligning with p99 windows. Collecting kernel-level metrics and batch histograms.

2026-03-12 12:28 - NimbusDocs (Customer): Provided repro harness and client logs. Observed that spikes often occur when a long request from internal QA runs concurrently with a burst of short streaming requests. Asked if a temporary workaround is possible.

2026-03-12 13:05 - Luca Moreno (SRE): Preliminary hypothesis: prefix-merge lag — when the coalescer receives a long request it begins waiting to merge prefix tokens for KV cache priming and inadvertently extends linger for coalesced short requests (head-of-line). This effect amplified by request prefetching policy and tenant weight misalignment. Plan: test by temporarily reducing coalescer linger for tenant nimbus-47 and disabling prefetching for long requests.
2026-03-12 15:47 - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer that we will attempt a non-disruptive config change in a canary subset of their pool and monitor impact. Customer approved.

2026-03-12 18:30 - Luca Moreno (SRE): Applied canary: coalescer.linger_ms lowered from 15 to 5 for tenant nimbus-47 on 2/3 of their nodes; prefetch_long_requests flag disabled. Early telemetry: p99 reduced to sub-800ms in canary nodes; overall tenant p99 decreased but still shows residual spikes tied to nodes not yet patched. Continuing rollout.

2026-03-13 09:10 - Engineering (Serving): Added note: KV cache warmup path was observed to hold shard locks during prefix-merge, blocking coalescer flush under specific sequence length heterogeneity. Raised a PR to release lock earlier in the warmup path. See related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2145

2026-03-14 11:22 - Luca Moreno (SRE): Full rollout completed to all tenant nodes. Post-rollout metrics: sustained p99 ~420ms, incidents rate reduced to 0/hour. Follow-ups planned: permanent config tuning, PR deployment for lock release, and a stress test to cover mixed short/long workload patterns.
investigation_notes: Correlation: p99 windows align with spikes in coalescer.flush_delay_ms and a sudden shift in batch-size histogram where many small requests are held until a long request arrived.
Hypothesis A: Prefetching policy for long requests triggers prefix-merge behavior that holds coalescer flush longer than configured linger_ms under certain interleavings.
Hypothesis B: Tenant weight misalignment caused the coalescer to treat the tenant as higher-priority and wait for larger batch composition, increasing head-of-line latency for short streams.
Observed: KV cache warmup path acquires a shard-level mutex while priming prefixes; when long request arrives it holds the mutex and stalls short-request flush callbacks on same coalescer thread.
Repro: Reproducer provided by customer reliably triggered p99 spikes when a single long request was injected every 25s into a steady stream of short requests at 12 rps across 100 connections.
Canary change: reduce coalescer.linger_ms and disable long-request prefetching reduced p99 at canary nodes from 2.7s -> 480ms.
Code change proposed: release KV warmup shard lock after prefix data is enqueued to coalescer instead of after synchronous priming completes (PR #2145).
resolution: Workaround applied: temporary coalescer config changes (linger_ms=5, disable prefetch_long_requests) rolled out to tenant nimbus-47; immediate p99 improvement observed. Root cause: interaction between prefix-merge/prefetching logic and KV cache warmup holding shard locks caused head-of-line delays for short streaming requests. Fix: merged PR to adjust KV warmup locking and updated coalescer flush logic to honor tenant short-stream priority. Deployed serving v1.8.3 with fix on 2026-03-14. Post-deploy monitoring shows p99 stable <500ms. Follow-ups: create automated regression test for mixed short/long workload, update runbook with recommended per-tenant defaults, add alerting on coalescer.flush_delay_ms anomaly. Customer notified and provided post-incident report.
